title: D1 fix round 5: merge_reviewed never raises on odd verdicts, review count frozen at gate time, single-review src fallback only, sweep covers ungated tasks, drop inert second_review, cheap filters first (from review T-0164)
spec:
Fix round for T-0160 (branch task/T-0160 at 2f37982 on goal/T-0109). Work in this task's worktree, cut from task/T-0160. Review T-0164 (opus) requested changes; items come from it. Scope: orchestrator/daemon.py and tests/test_daemon.py only.

1 HIGH merge_reviewed (≈line 430): never index stuck[0] without a guard, and make the verdict buckets exhaustive: a review that is done with verdict == "approve" counts as approved; a review that is done with ANY other verdict value (request_changes, missing, or an off-vocabulary string like "changes_requested") is treated as request_changes → hold src with hold_reason "review request_changes: <id> (<verdict>)"; queued/running = pending; failed/held = stuck. If none of approved/pending/stuck/rejected apply (should be impossible) → hold with hold_reason "review state unknown: <ids>" instead of raising. Wrap the per-task body in try/except that prints one stderr line and continues, so one task can never stop the sweep for the others. Tests: (a) c7 task, r1 approve + r2 done with verdict "changes_requested" → held, no exception, other tasks in the same tick still processed; (b) c5 task whose only review is done with an unrecognised verdict → held with that verdict in hold_reason.

2 MED gate() (≈line 414): persist the review count at gate time: stamp pipeline.reviews_expected = reviews_expected(t) alongside gated_at, and merge_reviewed reads pipeline.reviews_expected first, falling back to reviews_expected(t) only when the stamp is absent (tasks gated before this change). Test: gate at two_reviews_from=7 for a c7 task (stamp 2), then lower two_reviews_from to 8 in cfg → merge_reviewed still waits for 2 (no crash, no premature merge).

3 LOW merge_reviewed (≈line 389): use the src.review_verdict fallback only when the task has exactly one review; with two or more, each review's own result verdict decides. Test: c7 task, r1 approve (src.review_verdict approve written by the worker), r2 done without a verdict key → held (rejected), not merged.

4 LOW merge_reviewed (≈line 402): the sweep must also cover done execute tasks that have at least one review but no gated_at stamp (Planner-spawned reviews on a hand-gated task): condition = status done, not stale, not already_merged, has reviews; gated_at is not required. Test: done task without gated_at, one approve → merged.

5 LOW gate(): remove constraints.second_review (nothing reads it) and its test assertion; keep the second review's tier logic.

6 LOW gate() and merge_reviewed(): order the filters cheap-first: status/stale/pipeline checks before already_merged() (which shells out to git).

No new dependency. Commit on the task branch when green (`git add`, `git commit`). Finish with: summary, files changed, failures-only test output.
acceptance: merge_reviewed never raises: odd or missing verdicts on done reviews hold the task with a reason naming the review and verdict; one task's error cannot stop the sweep (tests a, b)
pipeline.reviews_expected is stamped at gate time and honoured at merge time; a later config change neither crashes nor merges early (test)
src.review_verdict fallback applies only to single-review tasks (test)
Done tasks with reviews but no gated_at are swept (test)
constraints.second_review removed with its assertion; filters ordered cheap-first (already_merged last)
uv run python -m unittest discover -q tests green; no new dependency; only daemon.py and tests/test_daemon.py change; committed on the task branch

result.summary:
Committed as `c593794` on `task/T-0169`.

## Summary
The fix-round changes for the T-0164 review items were already present, uncommitted, in the worktree. I verified each acceptance criterion against the diff, ran the full test suite, and committed.

- `merge_reviewed`/`_merge_reviewed_one` now buckets each review's verdict exhaustively (approved/rejected/pending/stuck/unknown), guards `stuck[0]` behind `if stuck:`, and wraps the per-task body in try/except so one bad task can't stop the sweep.
- `gate()` stamps `pipeline.reviews_expected` at gate time; `merge_reviewed` reads that stamp first, falling back to `reviews_expected(t)` only when absent.
- `src.review_verdict` fallback now only applies when `len(reviews) == 1`.
- The sweep no longer requires `gated_at`, so hand-gated tasks with reviews are covered.
- `constraints.second_review` and its test assertion removed.
- Filters in `gate()` and `merge_reviewed()` reordered cheap-first, `already_merged()` (git shell-out) last.

## Files changed
- `orchestrator/daemon.py`
- `tests/test_daemon.py`

```

OK
```
No failures (only harmless `ResourceWarning`s from sqlite in unrelated test fixtures). `.claude/hooks/tests-green.sh` also exited 0.
